name: ow2_default
description: Overwatch 2 HUD regions at 16:9, normalised (0..1). Calibrated against real gameplay. The OW2 HUD scales with resolution, so the normalised values hold from 360p to 4K. Adjust with tools/calibrate.py if language, colour-blind mode or a patch change positions and colours.

kills.name: kills
kills._note: centred on the crosshair: the kill skull is born at ~(0.50, 0.485)

killfeed.name: killfeed
killfeed._note: starts at 0.68 so it does not catch the scoreboard panel, which is fixed red. Starts at 0.02 and not 0.04 because the FIRST killfeed line is born at ~0.031 of the height: with the cut at 0.04 it came cut in half, and the cut line lost enough height for the killfeed detector not to recognise the plate.
killfeed._note_resolution: 960 enlarges nothing: the crop comes out at min(960, native width), so it is 'native up to a 3000px screen'. It was at 480, and on a 1440p recording that threw away 40% of the band's pixels. It costs: the killer's name needs them. At 480 the killfeed letters are 8 pixels tall and run into each other -- measured on the reference recording, none of the player's 3 lines came out whole. Icon matching changes with it too, for the better: at 480 the same recording yielded 7 lines with heroes who were not even in the match, and at native it yields coherent lines, with the same ability repeated over each line's life.

ult.name: ult
ult._note: the footer's ultimate button, centred at (0.50, 0.86). It is where the PLAYER's ultimate is seen: charged it becomes a white disc with the hero's icon, surrounded by a cyan ring; once used, it goes back to a dark ring with the percentage.

player.name: player
player._note: the player's own card in the bottom-left corner: level, emblem and the NAME. It is the only place on screen that says who is playing, and without it there is no knowing whose kill the killfeed announced. The band starts at 0.897 and not 0.885 on purpose: above that comes the health bar, and its ticks would pass the letter filter and form a 26-letter 'word' -- longer than any name. Measured on the reference recording (1440p): the name's letters sit between 0.902 and 0.924 of the height.

health.name: health
health._note: thin strip of the health bar, bottom-left corner

banner.name: banner
banner._note: footer strip where OW2 stacks the action banners (sleep, saved, orb...)

kills._note: The skull is an interface element: narrow magenta hue and high saturation. The scenery and the damage indicator fall in the same colour range -- the decision comes from shape, position and SIZE. min_area_frac is the most important filter: the skull takes 5-14% of the region and red splashes stay below 2.5%. Calibrated on 19 min of real gameplay (~91% precision).
kills._note_confirm: A skull only counts if a killfeed line appears near it: destroying a deployable (a Symmetra turret, a teleporter) draws the same skull and puts nothing in the killfeed. confirm_window_s = [seconds before, seconds after] the skull in which the line may appear; the killfeed ROI runs at 5 fps, so the line is seen up to 0.2 s late.

headshot._note: Critical hit: OW2 draws the hit marker in RED (a normal hit is white). It is four thick strokes in an X, centred on the crosshair, born small and growing for ~0.3s. The decision is not by colour -- it is by SHAPE: the four diagonals must be red and the four straight directions (up, down, left, right) must NOT. Without that second half the kill skull, which is also red and also born on the crosshair, became a headshot: it fills all eight directions.
headshot._note_measured: Measured on a real 2558x1438 recording: the X scores 0.81 at its peak and the scene stays at 0.06 at the 99th percentile. The crosshair is the centre of the SCREEN, and its position inside the crop comes from the ROI's own geometry -- there is no number to calibrate here.

death._note: Death = health dropping to zero and coming back full on the next frame (you start spectating a teammate), or the bar disappearing altogether (menu, round change). For the rules both cases mean the same: the streak was interrupted.

survival._note: Reads the health bar directly. The red vignette on the edges does NOT work: it is the damage-taken indicator and shows up in ~32% of frames in a real match.

ults._note: Three paths, and they answer different questions. The BUTTON path sees the player's own ultimate and is the only one that works without the user preparing anything. The killfeed path looks for enemy ultimate icons in templates/ults/ -- without those crops it emits nothing, on purpose. The audio path exists but ships off: in real gameplay it cannot tell an ultimate voice line from gunfire and explosions.

self._note: The player's own ultimate, read on the footer button. Charged = a WHITE disc with the hero's icon + a CYAN ring around it. Using the ultimate turns both off at once, so the event is the FALLING EDGE: the instant the button stops being charged.
self._note_conjunction: Both conditions hold together, never alone: D.Va's explosion fills the region with white without any cyan, and some maps' sky does the opposite. Measured on the test recordings, charged gives 0.12-0.17 of disc and 0.08-0.44 of cyan; any other frame stays below 0.03 on at least one of them.
self._note_timing: flicker_s stitches HUD blinks (one frame without the button is not a used ultimate). min_after_s requires the button to stay uncharged afterwards: charging again takes dozens of seconds, so an 'off and back' within 6s was the HUD disappearing, not an ultimate. Known side effect: D.Va and Dmon have two chained ultimates (Self-Destruct and then Call Mech); when both fall within min_after_s -- in the practice range, where charging is instant -- only the second becomes an event.
self._note_charge: min_charged_s exists because the button is not the only bright round thing passing through this window: the kill cam draws a disc with the killer's face, and explosion or sky flashes also fill the region. All of those last 1 to 3 frames. Measured on 27 min of real matches (Ana 16min + Sigma 11min): real ultimates stay charged 2.8s to 43s, and the 10 short stretches were all false. The number was calibrated on MATCHES, on purpose -- in the practice range charging is instant, and letting those clips decide is what let 10 false ones through before.

killfeed._note: Each killfeed line is '<killer> <ability icon> > <victim>'. The colour does NOT say the team: measured on the reference recording, the same player shows up on the blue plate of one line and the red of another -- blue is the killer, red is the victim, on both sides of the match. Only the name written on the blue plate answers who it was, and that is what `name_threshold` checks against the footer card.
killfeed._note_icon: The icon lives in the gap between the two plates, and the '>' takes the end of that gap. The window used to stop at 0.66 of the gap to leave the '>' out; on a real 1080p match the '>' of a gun kill fell inside that window in most frames (the gap is narrower without an icon), so a gun kill offered a clean '>' to be matched every frame. Now the window runs to 1.0 and the glyph step erases the rightmost piece of the mark, which is always the '>'. An ultimate shows up as a white disc with a black drawing; a regular ability, as a white drawing in a dark box.
killfeed._note_measured: Measured with the black-and-white glyph, before the comparison in grey: on a real recording the right icon scored 0.65-0.93 and the runner-up 0.27-0.55. The grey comparison raises every score (right and wrong alike), so those numbers do not carry over -- see _note_threshold.
killfeed._note_threshold: The icon is compared in shades of grey and at the size it was seen (IconBank.rank), which raises every score, so the old 0.65 no longer means anything. 0.85 is PROVISIONAL: it comes from synthetic icons degraded to 8-32 px with JPEG compression, where a line's best frame for the right icon passes it at 16 px and up and gun-kill gaps stay at 0.25-0.35 on the sample video. It must be checked on a real match before it is trusted -- the old rule (precision 100%, recall 7/11) was measured on one. What keeps a gun kill out is now mostly the vote below, not this number.
killfeed._note_votes: A line names an ability only if that ability was the best match in at least icon_min_votes frames AND in icon_vote_share of the voting frames, and only frames whose best match reaches icon_vote_floor vote at all. A gap with no icon (a gun kill) matches something different in each frame, and poorly; a real icon wins frame after frame. Measured on a real 1080p Ana match (16 min, 153 lines checked by eye): tracks there are short -- the plates' edges jump with the scenery behind them and a line often splits into 2-4 tracks -- so min_votes 3 lost kills whose track had 2 frames, and without the floor a 13-frame blade at 0.97 lost its line to 20 frames of a crop that had landed on hero portraits. No gun line named an ability with these values.
killfeed._note_min_side: Glyphs smaller than icon_min_side_px (the drawing's own height or width, in pixels of the crop) do not vote. On synthetic icons at 8 px the grey comparison named half the lines -- and gave 18% of them the WRONG ability, consistently, because at that size two drawings really are the same blob. Voting does not catch that kind of error. From ~10 px on the gate barely costs anything. It is roughly a recording below 480p.
killfeed._note_hold: hold_s holds the line count for a moment: the icon crop fails on isolated frames (the line slides in, and compression eats the drawing), and without it each failure split one line into two kills. It only delays the count's fall -- it does not invent lines. 1s was nowhere near: in a real match the crop of ONE line fails for 3 to 5 seconds in a row, and the same kill came out 2, 3 or 4 times. 7s is a line's life on screen, and it is what the 1s-to-12s sweep points to: from 5s on Ana's result stops changing, and 7s still removes the old line that came back as a new kill when a more recent line pushed it down. Holding longer never lost a real kill -- two with the same ability raise the count to 2, and that is already a rising edge.
killfeed._note_slide: slide_s is how long the line takes to finish coming in. In that beginning the plates are still opening -- on a real recording one of the outer edges moves 16 to 20 pixels from one frame to the next -- and only the inner edges, which surround the icon, serve to recognise the line. After that time the outer ones count again, and they are what separate two kills by the same player.
killfeed._note_name: 0.40 sits in the middle of the gap. Measured on the reference recording, with 81 killfeed lines checked one by one: the player's 3 lines score 0.59, 0.66 and 0.66, and the highest score among the 78 others is 0.21 -- and it belongs to MATEUSKCZ, which happens to have the same 9 letters as CENOURAET. Names of different lengths score 0 on their own.

banner._note: The footer shows several banners with the same colour and shape (SAVED BY, ORB OF HARMONY, GAINED FROM, ... STUNNED BY, PUT ... TO SLEEP). Colour and geometry find the banner; what says WHICH ability is the ICON on the left end, compared with the templates in config/shapes/. Icon and not text on purpose: text changes with the language, the icon does not.
banner._note_colour: Two colour ranges because the banner colour changes from recording to recording: cyan in an Ana match, green in a Sigma one. They are searched SEPARATELY (one mask per colour) -- added together, one recording's bluish scenery stuck to the green banner and made the banner vanish as a rectangle.
banner._note_calibration: Validated on two real recordings, with each template trained only on the first half of its video: Ana 16 min -> 11/11 darts, 0 false; Sigma 11 min -> 23/23 rocks, 0 false (12 never seen in training). The threshold is per ability (see each one): a single number forced a choice between missing darts and accepting false rocks.

abilities._note: Ana's sleep dart: 'PUT <hero> TO SLEEP'. At 0.85: 11/11 darts in 16 min of her gameplay, no false ones; and no trigger on the Sigma recording.

Sigma's rock: '<hero> STUNNED BY ACCRETION'. At 0.92: 23/23 rocks in 11 min, no false ones. A higher threshold than the dart's because this icon is full and contrasted, and matches high even with neighbouring banners ('GAINED FROM').

banner._note_section_threshold: match_threshold here is only the default for whoever does not declare their own.
